answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can vote or claim rewards. The protocol caps influence by stake and penalizes accounts whose coordinated actions violate rules, making it costly to split one identity into many: every fake agent needs its own capital at risk. A relic token on a mesa is still hollow collateral if it can be minted freely, so the stake must be scarce and costly to acquire.
